strengths: Well-motivated problem formulation addressing genuine limitations of single-answer evaluation benchmarks; compelling motivation grounded in developmental psychology and social science
Rigorous dataset construction with three-stage pipeline, high inter-annotator agreement (AC2=0.84-0.91), and comprehensive diversity analysis demonstrating avoidance of generation collapse

Comprehensive evaluation across diverse model architectures, prompting strategies, and evaluation settings with valuable decomposition analysis separating atomic plausibility, operator grounding, and distractor effects

Clear and reproducible findings: sharp performance collapse on NEITHER/NOR (13.9% for LLaMA-3.1-8B) vs. commonsenseQA baseline (72.2%), consistent across open-weight and proprietary models, with fine-tuned models achieving 83-95% F1

Excellent reproducibility with public dataset/code, detailed prompt templates, complete training configurations, and interpretable error analysis identifying systematic failure patterns (negation inversion, plausibility dominance)
Well-written paper with clear presentation and effective demonstration that existing benchmarks overestimate compositional reasoning capabilities
weaknesses: Heavy reliance on GPT-4o-mini for generation and refinement with only 50% of test set human-validated; non-validated subset quality is unknown and NEITHER/NOR label accuracy (73.6%) is notably lower than other operators, suggesting systematic issues inadequately analyzed

Limited scope: only three operators evaluated; findings limited to CommonsenseQA domain; unclear how well insights transfer to other compositional structures or broader commonsense domains despite claims about compositional reasoning

Insufficient human evaluation: only 10 examples per condition (40 total) with no inter-rater agreement reported; insufficient for robust human-model comparison or validation of claimed benchmark solvability

Limited actionable insights: paper documents failure modes but provides minimal guidance on improvement pathways; decomposition analysis identifies interactions but doesn't explain underlying mechanisms or suggest solutions

Incomplete analysis of prompting strategies: chain-of-thought only evaluated for one model, underperforms on NEITHER/NOR (worse than zero-shot in Table 6), with no investigation into why reasoning strategies fail

Lack of statistical rigor: no confidence intervals, significance tests, or variance estimates; given small human evaluation sample and multiple model comparisons, statistical support would strengthen claims

Somewhat expected findings: logical reasoning failures in LLMs are well-documented; the negation-specific collapse, while clearly demonstrated, aligns with existing work on systematic reasoning limitations

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing a genuine gap: existing benchmarks fail to evaluate compositional plausibility judgments and whether models recognize jointly plausible, exclusive, or implausible statement pairs

Rigorous three-stage dataset construction pipeline combining neural generation with human refinement and validation, with high inter-annotator agreement (AC2 ≥ 0.84) using theoretically grounded awareness-consensus framework

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across diverse model families (encoder-only, encoder-decoder, decoder-only LLMs, proprietary models) under multiple settings (0/1/2/3-shot, CoT, fine-tuning) revealing consistent systematic weaknesses

Sophisticated decomposition analysis (Table 8) that isolates atomic plausibility estimation, operator grounding, and distractor competition, showing task difficulty arises from their interaction rather than any single component

Concrete error analysis with specific failure patterns (single-statement dominance, semantic similarity confusion, negation inversion) that provide actionable insights into model compositional reasoning limitations

Fine-tuned models achieving 83-95% F1 across operators confirms benchmark is learnable with supervision, validating that zero/few-shot failures reflect inference-time limitations rather than dataset artifacts
Clear presentation with excellent supporting materials (detailed prompts, training configurations, annotation guidelines, diversity metrics) enabling reproducibility and future work
Strategic experimental design with human-validated vs. non-validated splits and operator-specific vs. mixed conditions that enables nuanced analysis
weaknesses: Restrictive operator space: limited to three basic operators (AND, OR, NEITHER/NOR) without exploring implication, exclusive-or, temporal reasoning, or conditional structures, significantly constraining scope of compositional reasoning studied

Modest dataset scale with 19,996 instances, 2,000 test examples, and only 1,000 human-validated examples; for a benchmark paper, larger scale would increase impact and enable more robust statistical analysis
Entire dataset derived from CommonsenseQA, inheriting source biases and limiting diversity of commonsense domains; single-source derivation reduces novelty and generalizability
Very small human evaluation with only 10 examples per condition (40 total), insufficient to draw strong conclusions about human performance gaps; human/model performance differences could be noise

Variable label quality with NEITHER/NOR achieving only 73.6% accuracy versus 89.2% for AND and 96.4% for OR, raising questions about annotation difficulty or task definition; impact on conclusions about model failures unclear
Shallow composition structure with only two-statement pairs; no exploration of 3+ statement compositions or nested logical structures limits insights about complex real-world reasoning
No transfer analysis to downstream tasks (QA, dialogue, planning); impact on real applications remains unexplored, limiting practical significance beyond the benchmark itself
Limited chain-of-thought evaluation (only LLaMA-3.1-8B) when CoT could plausibly help with NEITHER/NOR weakness; broader CoT analysis across models would strengthen conclusions

Potential LLM-generation artifacts: atomic options generated and refined by GPT-4o-mini could introduce systematic biases; while diversity metrics are provided, alternative generation approaches not explored
Missing statistical rigor: no confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars reported despite small test set (2,000 examples) and operator-specific performance variations
